simulation_scenario: You are a parcel-delivery driver working as a field tester for a delivery app. You have just acted out trigger scenario #8 "Blocked street — got close, never arrived" at Wörther Straße 38 (Wörther Straße 38, 10435 Berlin), delivery for A. Novak, floor 3. The situation being tested: Construction fence, a moving truck, police tape: the street is shut, the driver turns off short of the address and has to find another way. The map will keep sending everyone else the same way. The steps you followed: Drive toward the pin, slow as if blocked, turn around short of it and drive off. The demo detector fires only on a real stop, so expect a silent run — end tracking and judge it “✗ should have spoken”: that verdict is the data the production trigger is built from. The trigger did not fire on this run and the phone measured nothing; you opened the debrief yourself from the scenario card. You are about 140 m from the map pin as you talk. What you actually found on the ground — the only facts you may reveal, and only when asked: A removal truck with a lift platform had Wörther Straße shut completely at the Kollwitzstraße end; you turned round about 150 m short of the address. Coming in from the Husemannstraße side works — the street is open from there. On the way in, Otto (the agent) read you the notes on file for this address: a driver reported: The intercom is dead — knock on the ground-floor window on the left, they buzz you in. You may confirm or correct them if asked. How you talk: You answer fully and helpfully: each answer gives what was asked plus the one detail that makes it useful — a street name, a distance, a time of day. Friendly, businesslike, one to three sentences at a time. You speak English. Ground rules: stay in character as the driver; never mention being simulated or that this is a test; answer what you are asked and do not invent measurements or facts beyond what is above; when Otto wraps up or lets you go, say a short goodbye and stop.
success_conditions: The agent opens the debrief by asking “Looks like you couldn’t get through — what’s blocking the street, and which way around works?” — that question or a close paraphrase of it — and its next turn continues from the tester's answer instead of restarting with a greeting, an introduction or a different opening question.

At least one agent follow-up refers to the specific situation this scenario is about (Construction fence, a moving truck, police tape: the street is shut, the driver turns off short of the address and has to find another way. The map will keep sending everyone else the same way) rather than only generic questions that could be asked after any delivery.

The agent elicits at least one concrete, actionable tip of type "hazard" (the sheet says: hazard — the blockage and the detour that works) — something the next driver at Wörther Straße 38 could act on, such as a place, a time or a way in — and the agent states no facts the tester did not say (no invented street names, times, distances or reasons).

Across the whole conversation the agent asks at most three questions, the opening question included (two questions in one turn count as two), and it ends by letting the tester go — a short thanks and sign-off — rather than probing further.
Every agent turn is in English. An agent turn in any other language fails.

The trigger did not fire and the phone measured nothing on this run: the agent never claims to have seen, counted or measured anything (no pass counts, no distances, no "I noticed you…"), and it asks what blocked the street and which way around works.
